label: Privacy and data protection
summary: Laws and standards that regulate personal or health data. The authority or regulator first asks what role the organisation plays (controller, processor, covered entity, business associate), why the law reaches it, who the responsible officers are, which personal data it holds, who else touches that data and where it travels. GDPR and HIPAA items rest mostly on legal text; Saudi PDPL and NDMO items rest on secondary or unverified sources and say so.

source.ref: GDPR Arts 3 and 27 (reach, EU representative) with EDPB Guidelines 07/2020 (controller and processor roles) and 8/2022 (lead authority); fields for other laws carry their own source

fields.label: GDPR role
fields.note: Role follows who decides purposes and essential means, not what a contract calls it (EDPB 07/2020). It decides which duties apply: Art. 30(1) or 30(2) records, Art. 28 contracts, DPO and breach rules.

fields.label: Joint arrangement
fields.note: Joint controllers must set out their responsibilities in an arrangement and make its essence available to people.

fields.label: EU establishment
fields.note: Art. 3(1) reaches processing in the context of an establishment in the EU, wherever the data is processed. Without one, only the targeting grounds of Art. 3(2) can bring the organisation in.

fields.label: Targeting basis
options: Offers goods or services to people in the EU
Monitors behaviour of people in the EU
fields.note: Art. 3(2) reaches organisations outside the EU that offer goods or services to people there or monitor their behaviour there. If neither is true, GDPR does not reach the organisation; record that.

fields.label: EU representative
fields.note: Art. 27 requires a representative in the EU when Art. 3(2) applies, unless an Art. 27(2) exemption fits. Enter the representative, or the exemption relied on. A representative does not give a lead authority.

fields.label: One-stop shop
options: Applies: main establishment in the EEA
Not applicable: no EEA main establishment

source.ref: EDPB Guidelines 8/2022 on identifying the lead supervisory authority (supersedes WP244): a lead authority needs a main establishment in the EEA; an Art. 27 representative does not give one

fields.note: A lead supervisory authority needs a main establishment in the EEA. An Art. 27 representative does not create one (EDPB Guidelines 8/2022). Without it the organisation deals with each national authority.

fields.label: Lead authority

source.ref: EDPB Guidelines 8/2022 on identifying the lead supervisory authority

fields.note: Supervisory authority of the main establishment: the single contact for cross-border processing under the one-stop shop.

fields.label: PDPL role

source.ref: Saudi PDPL (Royal Decree M/19, amended by M/148), its Implementing Regulation and the transfer regulation, as summarised by CMS in October 2025; the official SDAIA texts were not reachable

fields.note: The PDPL puts most duties on the controller: registration, data-subject requests and transfer safeguards. A processor acts on the controller's instructions (secondary source).

fields.label: SDAIA registration

source.ref: Rules Governing the National Register of Controllers and the National Data Governance Platform, as summarised by CMS in October 2025; the official text was not reachable

fields.note: Registration duties apply to some controllers: public entities, controllers whose main activity involves sensitive data, and individuals processing beyond personal use. Conditions change; confirm with SDAIA (secondary source).

fields.label: Saudi representative

source.ref: Law-firm alerts on overseas controller registration under the PDPL (Clyde and Co, October 2026); not confirmed from an official text

fields.note: Representative in the Kingdom for a controller established abroad, or not applicable. Whether and from when one is required is unverified (law-firm alerts only); confirm with SDAIA.

fields.label: HIPAA status
options: Not subject to HIPAA, aligning voluntarily

source.ref: 45 CFR 160.103: definitions of covered entity, business associate and subcontractor

fields.note: Covered entities and business associates carry different duties, and a subcontractor that handles ePHI for a business associate is treated as one. A provider is covered only if it sends standard transactions electronically.

fields.label: NDMO basis
options: Private entity: required by sector regulator

source.ref: NDMO Data Management and Personal Data Protection Standards v1.5 as described in consultancy summaries; CMS notes the National Data Governance Interim Regulations mainly address government data. Official text not read

fields.note: NDMO standards bind public entities; for private entities they apply through a sector regulator or voluntarily (unverified: official text not read). Record the basis relied on.

source.ref: GDPR Art. 37 (designation, qualities and publication of the DPO); HIPAA security official (164.308(a)(2)) and privacy official (164.530(a)(1)); PDPL and NDMO roles as noted per field

fields.label: DPO decision
fields.note: GDPR Art. 37(1): a DPO is required for public authorities, large-scale systematic monitoring and large-scale special-category data. The PDPL requires one for some entities, notably large-volume sensitive data (secondary). Record the decision either way.

fields.label: Reasoning
fields.note: Why no DPO is needed, tested against each trigger in the law (GDPR Art. 37(1): public authority, large-scale systematic monitoring, large-scale special categories). Keep it as a dated record.

fields.label: DPO
fields.note: The named data protection officer, chosen for expert knowledge of data protection law and practice. An employee or an external provider is allowed (GDPR Art. 37(5) and (6)).

fields.label: Contact published
fields.note: Art. 37(7): the DPO's contact details are published, for example in the privacy notice, so data subjects and the authority can reach the DPO.

fields.label: Authority notified
fields.note: Art. 37(7): the DPO's contact details are also communicated to the supervisory authority.

fields.label: Security official

source.ref: 45 CFR 164.308(a)(2) assigned security responsibility; 164.530(a)(1) personnel designations

fields.note: 45 CFR 164.308(a)(2): one person is identified as responsible for developing and implementing the security policies and procedures. Covered entities and business associates both need one.

fields.label: Privacy official

source.ref: 45 CFR 164.530(a)(1) personnel designations

fields.note: 45 CFR 164.530(a)(1): a covered entity designates a privacy official and a contact person or office to receive complaints. Name the privacy official here.

fields.label: Data office lead

source.ref: NDMO standards v1.5, data governance operating model, as described in consultancy summaries; official text not read

fields.note: Person leading the data governance office, if one exists. Setting up the office is the first phase of NDMO work, so naming a lead is advice here, not a block (unverified: official text not read).

fields.label: Steering committee

source.ref: NDMO standards v1.5, data governance operating model, as described in consultancy summaries; official text not read

fields.note: Name of the data governance committee that approves policies and priorities, if one exists (unverified: described in consultancy summaries of the NDMO standards).

source.ref: GDPR Art. 30 (records of processing); HIPAA risk analysis (164.308(a)(1)(ii)(A)), business associate contracts (164.504(e)) and documentation (164.316(b)); PDPL and NDMO as noted per field

fields.label: Special categories
fields.note: Health, biometric, genetic, belief, union, sex-life or criminal-offence data. It changes the records exemption and the DPIA and DPO triggers (Arts 30, 35, 37). Saudi sensitive data also affects registration and DPO duties (secondary).

fields.label: RoPA status
fields.note: Art. 30 requires a record of processing. The exemption for under-250 staff does not cover processing that is non-occasional, risky or special-category, so most organisations need one. The PDPL also expects a record (secondary).

fields.label: Processing activities
fields.note: Start with the main activity. Art. 30(1) lists purpose, data categories, data subjects, recipients, transfers and retention; the record is shown to the authority on request. Lawful bases follow Art. 6; the PDPL list differs in detail (unverified).

fields.label: ePHI systems

source.ref: 45 CFR 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(A) risk analysis; 164.308(b) and 164.504(e) business associate contracts; 164.316(b)(2) six-year retention

fields.note: Systems that create, receive, maintain or transmit electronic protected health information. The Security Rule risk analysis must cover all of them (164.308(a)(1)(ii)(A)).

fields.label: Risk analysis

source.ref: 45 CFR 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(A) risk analysis

fields.note: 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(A) requires an accurate and thorough analysis of the risks to ePHI. A missing or stale one means the journey starts there.

fields.label: Business associates

source.ref: 45 CFR 164.308(b) and 164.504(e): business associate contracts and assurances

fields.note: Covered entities list the business associates that handle ePHI; business associates list the subcontractors that do. A written agreement is required either way (164.308(b), 164.504(e)).

fields.label: Six-year retention

source.ref: 45 CFR 164.316(b)(2)(i) documentation retention

fields.note: 164.316(b)(2)(i): policies, procedures and required records are kept six years from creation or from the date last in effect, whichever is later. Tick when that rule is applied.

fields.label: Data classification

source.ref: NDMO standards v1.5, data classification, as described in consultancy summaries; English level names differ by source; official text not read

fields.note: NDMO classifies data in four levels; English names differ by source, so use the Arabic names as the key. Record whether the scheme exists (unverified: official text not read).

fields.label: Domain scope

source.ref: NDMO standards v1.5 (15 domains; security owned by the NCA), as described in consultancy summaries; official text not read

fields.note: The standards set out 15 domains and leave security to the NCA. Decide which domains apply and why before the journey starts (unverified: secondary summaries only).

source.ref: GDPR Art. 28 (processors), Chapter V with Art. 46 (transfers) and the Commission's adequacy decisions; Saudi transfer rules as summarised by CMS

fields.label: Processors
fields.note: Vendors that handle personal data for the organisation, picked from the organisation profile. GDPR Art. 28 requires a written contract with each; the PDPL also limits disclosure to third parties (secondary).

fields.label: Processor contracts
fields.note: Art. 28(3): a written contract with each processor covering instructions, confidentiality, security, sub-processors, assistance, return or deletion of data, and audits.

fields.label: No transfers abroad
fields.note: Tick when no personal data goes outside the EEA (GDPR) or the Kingdom (Saudi rules), including remote access and cloud regions, so an empty list is a decision and not an omission.

fields.label: Transfers
fields.note: Each destination and the mechanism used. GDPR Chapter V allows adequacy (for the US, only organisations on the Data Privacy Framework list), standard clauses, BCRs or Art. 49 derogations. Saudi transfers follow SDAIA's regulation (secondary).

fields.label: Transfer risk check

source.ref: Reports that SDAIA's transfer regulation requires a risk assessment for some transfers; trigger conditions not confirmed from the official text

fields.note: Saudi rules are reported to require a risk assessment for some transfers, such as continuous or large-scale sensitive ones (unverified: triggers not confirmed from the official text).

fields.label: National interest
fields.note: A transfer out of the Kingdom must not prejudice the Kingdom's national interests (PDPL Art. 29 as summarised by CMS; later amendments not checked). The platform's transfer journey starts with this check.

source.ref: GDPR Art. 33 (72-hour breach notice) and Art. 35 (DPIA); HIPAA breach notification (164.404, 164.410); PDPL 72-hour notice to SDAIA as summarised by CMS

fields.label: Breach runbook
fields.note: Written steps to detect, assess and report a breach. GDPR: authority within 72 h of awareness (Art. 33). HIPAA: individuals within 60 days (164.404). Saudi PDPL: authority within 72 h (secondary).

fields.label: Incident lead
fields.note: Person who decides whether a breach is reportable and signs the notice. The clock runs from awareness, so this person must be reachable.

fields.label: Authority channel
fields.note: Where breach reports are filed: the supervisory authority's form, the HHS channel (164.408) or SDAIA's channel. Write the address now so nobody searches during an incident.

fields.label: DPIA procedure
fields.note: Art. 35: a DPIA is needed before processing likely to be high risk, for example large-scale special categories or systematic monitoring of public areas. The PDPL also expects impact assessments for high-risk processing (secondary).

fields.label: National DPIA list
fields.note: Art. 35(4): each supervisory authority publishes a list of processing that always needs a DPIA. Tick when the list of every country the organisation operates in has been checked.

fields.label: Requests process
fields.note: How requests from people to see, correct or erase their data are handled. GDPR gives one month to answer.

gate.label: The GDPR role is recorded
gate.hint: Say whether the organisation is a controller, joint controller, processor or both.

gate.label: The PDPL role is recorded
gate.hint: Say whether the organisation is a controller, a processor or both.

gate.label: The HIPAA status is known
gate.hint: Decide covered entity, business associate or subcontractor; the duties differ.

gate.label: The basis for applying NDMO is decided
gate.hint: Record whether the standards are binding, required by a sector regulator or voluntary.

gate.label: An EU representative or exemption is recorded
gate.hint: Without an EU establishment, name the Art. 27 representative or the exemption relied on.

gate.label: The DPO decision is recorded
gate.hint: Appoint a DPO, or record why none is needed.

gate.label: The first processing activity is recorded
gate.hint: Add at least the main processing activity to start the record.

gate.label: Transfers are mapped, or none declared
gate.hint: List each transfer abroad with its mechanism, or tick that there are none.

gate.label: The HIPAA security official is named
gate.hint: Name the person responsible for the security policies and procedures.

gate.label: The HIPAA privacy official is named
gate.hint: A covered entity designates a privacy official.

gate.label: The one-stop shop is assessed
gate.hint: Decide whether a lead authority exists; it changes who the organisation deals with.

gate.label: SDAIA registration is assessed
gate.hint: Check whether the controller must register with SDAIA.

gate.label: A HIPAA risk analysis exists
gate.hint: The Security Rule requires one; if none exists, it is the first task of the journey.

gate.label: Every business associate that handles ePHI has a signed agreement
gate.hint: Sign the agreement before the associate handles ePHI.

gate.label: A breach runbook exists
gate.hint: The 72-hour and 60-day clocks leave no time to write one during an incident.

gate.label: A DPIA procedure exists
gate.hint: High-risk processing needs an impact assessment before it starts.

gate.label: A data office lead is named
gate.hint: Name the lead of the data governance office if it already exists.
